claim: An estimated 71 million people are chronically infected with hepatitis C virus worldwide.
source: Infection with hepatitis C virus (HCV), a positive strand RNA virus of the Flaviviridae family, represents a major health problem, with an estimated 71 million chronically infected patients worldwide (WHO, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to WHO, 2017

claim: In the absence of treatment, 15–30% of individuals with chronic HCV infection develop serious complications including cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma and liver failure.
source: In the absence of treatment, 15–30% of individuals with chronic HCV infection develop serious complications including cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma and liver failure (Shepard et al., 2005; Alter and Seeff, 2000; Li et al., 2015; Drummer, 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Seven major genotypes of HCV have been described, further divided into several subtypes.
source: Seven major genotypes of HCV have been described, further divided into several subtypes (Simmonds, 2004; Smith et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Simmonds, 2004 and Smith et al., 2014

claim: Within each infected individual, multiple distinct HCV variants co-exist as quasispecies.
source: Moreover, within each infected individual, multiple distinct HCV variants co-exist as quasipecies (Farci et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Farci et al., 2000

claim: Inter-host and intra-host HCV evolution is shaped by multiple forces, including human immune pressure.
source: Inter-host and intra-host HCV evolution is shaped by multiple forces, including human immune pressure (Merani et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Merani et al., 2011

claim: Ansari et al. (2017) identified associations between viral variants and human polymorphisms in the interferon lambda (IFN-λ) and HLA regions in a cohort of individuals of white ancestry predominantly infected with genotype 3a HCV.
source: Ansari et al. (2017) used this approach to analyze a cohort of individuals of white ancestry predominantly infected with genotype 3a HCV; they identified associations between viral variants and human polymorphisms in the interferon lambda (IFN-λ) and HLA regions, demonstrating an impact of both innate and acquired immunity on HCV sequence variation during chronic infection.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ansari et al., 2017

claim: The rs12979860 variant showed the strongest correlation with treatment-induced clearance of HCV infection.
source: The rs12979860 variant, which is located 3 kb upstream of IL28B (encoding IFN-λ3) and lies within intron 1 of IFNL4, showed the strongest correlation with treatment-induced clearance of infection in the first report (Ge et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ge et al., 2009

claim: rs12979860 is a marker for a dinucleotide insertion/deletion polymorphism, IFNL4 rs368234815 [ΔG > TT], which causes a frameshift that abrogates IFN-λ4 protein production.
source: More recent studies have shown that rs12979860 is in fact a marker for a dinucleotide insertion/deletion polymorphism, IFNL4 rs368234815 [ΔG > TT], which causes a frameshift that abrogates IFN-λ4 protein production (Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Prokunina-Olsson et al., 2013

claim: The two variants rs12979860 and rs368234815 are in strong linkage disequilibrium in European and Asian populations (r2 = 0.98 in CEU and 1.00 in CHB and JPT).
source: The two variants (rs12979860 and rs368234815) are in strong linkage disequilibrium in European and Asian populations (r2 = 0.98 in CEU and 1.00 in CHB and JPT): the rs12979860 C allele, associated with a higher rate of spontaneous HCV clearance and better response to interferon-based treatment, is found on the same haplotype as the rs368234815 TT allele and is thus tagging the absence of IFN-λ4 protein.
evidence: Supported by established knowledge of linkage disequilibrium patterns

claim: The rs12979860 C allele is associated with a higher rate of spontaneous HCV clearance and better response to interferon-based treatment.
source: The two variants (rs12979860 and rs368234815) are in strong linkage disequilibrium in European and Asian populations (r2 = 0.98 in CEU and 1.00 in CHB and JPT): the rs12979860 C allele, associated with a higher rate of spontaneous HCV clearance and better response to interferon-based treatment, is found on the same haplotype as the rs368234815 TT allele and is thus tagging the absence of IFN-λ4 protein.
evidence: Supported by established knowledge from previous studies

claim: The study analyzed paired human and viral genetic data for 8,729 HCV-infected patients participating in various clinical trials of anti-HCV drugs.
source: We obtained paired human and viral genetic data for 8,729 HCV-infected patients participating in various clinical trials of anti-HCV drugs.
evidence: Describes the study sample

claim: The study samples were heterogeneous in terms of self-reported ancestry (85% Europeans, 13% Asians and 2% Africans).
source: The samples were heterogeneous in terms of self-reported ancestry (85% Europeans, 13% Asians and 2% Africans) and HCV genotypes, with a majority of HCV genotype 1a, 2a and 3a (Table 1).
evidence: Describes the demographic composition of the study sample

claim: The study included a majority of HCV genotype 1a, 2a and 3a.
source: The samples were heterogeneous in terms of self-reported ancestry (85% Europeans, 13% Asians and 2% Africans) and HCV genotypes, with a majority of HCV genotype 1a, 2a and 3a (Table 1).
evidence: Describes the viral genotype distribution in the study sample

claim: Deep sequencing was performed on the coding regions of the HCV non-structural proteins NS3, NS4A, NS5A and NS5B.
source: We genotyped the human SNP rs12979860 and performed deep sequencing of the coding regions of the HCV non-structural proteins NS3, NS4A, NS5A and NS5B (Bartenschlager et al., 2004).
evidence: Describes the sequencing methodology used in the study

claim: A binary variable was generated for each alternate amino acid, indicating the presence or absence of that allele in a given sample (N = 10,681).
source: A binary variable was generated for each alternate amino acid, indicating the presence or absence of that allele in a given sample (N = 10,681).
evidence: Describes the data processing methodology

claim: Only amino acids that were present in at least 0.3% of the samples (N = 4,022) were used for the analysis.
source: For the analysis, we used only amino acids that were present in at least 0.3% of the samples (N = 4,022).
evidence: Describes the filtering criteria for amino acid variants

claim: Highly significant associations were observed between rs12979860 and HCV amino acid variables for each HCV genotype examined.
source: We observed highly significant associations between rs12979860 and HCV amino acid variables for each HCV genotype that we examined (Figure 1, Table 2).
evidence: Supported by data presented in Figure 1 and Table 2

claim: The highest number of significant associations was detected in the largest group of patients, infected with genotype 1a, most likely reflecting an effect of sample size on statistical power.
source: The highest number of significant associations was detected in the largest group of patients, infected with genotype 1a, most likely reflecting an effect of sample size on statistical power.
evidence: Inference based on the observed pattern of associations and sample sizes

claim: Most associations were specific to a single viral genotype.
source: Most associations were specific to a single viral genotype; however, some associations were significant across genotypes.
evidence: Describes the pattern of associations observed in the data

claim: Two strong associations were observed between rs12979860 and amino acid variables at position 2576 in viral protein NS5B, with the T allele associating with proline in genotypes 1a (p=1.5×10−10), 2b (p=5.4×10−15), 3a (p=8.3×10−12) and 4a (p=1.2×10−7).
source: As an example, two strong associations were observed between rs12979860 and amino acid variables at position 2576 in viral protein NS5B, with the T allele associating with proline in genotypes 1a (p=1.5×10−10), 2b (p=5.4×10−15), 3a (p=8.3×10−12) and 4a (p=1.2×10−7), and the C allele associating with alanine in genotypes 1a (p=1.2×10−11), 2a (p=3.8×10−6), 2b (p=4.02×10−8) and 3a (p=1.04×10−14).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: The C allele of rs12979860 associates with alanine at position 2576 in genotypes 1a (p=1.2×10−11), 2a (p=3.8×10−6), 2b (p=4.02×10−8) and 3a (p=1.04×10−14).
source: As an example, two strong associations were observed between rs12979860 and amino acid variables at position 2576 in viral protein NS5B, with the T allele associating with proline in genotypes 1a (p=1.5×10−10), 2b (p=5.4×10−15), 3a (p=8.3×10−12) and 4a (p=1.2×10−7), and the C allele associating with alanine in genotypes 1a (p=1.2×10−11), 2a (p=3.8×10−6), 2b (p=4.02×10−8) and 3a (p=1.04×10−14).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: The study replicated previously reported associations between IFNL4 variation and valine at position 2570 in NS5B (p=5.5×10−20) in patients infected with genotype 3a.
source: In patients infected with genotype 3a, we replicated the previously reported associations (Ansari et al., 2017) between IFNL4 variation and valine at position 2570 in NS5B (p=5.5×10−20), histidine at position 2991 in NS5B (p=4.6×10−12) and asparagine at position 2414 in NS5A (p=2.4×10−7).
evidence: Replicates findings from Ansari et al., 2017 with new data

claim: The study replicated previously reported associations between IFNL4 variation and histidine at position 2991 in NS5B (p=4.6×10−12) in patients infected with genotype 3a.
source: In patients infected with genotype 3a, we replicated the previously reported associations (Ansari et al., 2017) between IFNL4 variation and valine at position 2570 in NS5B (p=5.5×10−20), histidine at position 2991 in NS5B (p=4.6×10−12) and asparagine at position 2414 in NS5A (p=2.4×10−7).
evidence: Replicates findings from Ansari et al., 2017 with new data

claim: The study replicated previously reported associations between IFNL4 variation and asparagine at position 2414 in NS5A (p=2.4×10−7) in patients infected with genotype 3a.
source: In patients infected with genotype 3a, we replicated the previously reported associations (Ansari et al., 2017) between IFNL4 variation and valine at position 2570 in NS5B (p=5.5×10−20), histidine at position 2991 in NS5B (p=4.6×10−12) and asparagine at position 2414 in NS5A (p=2.4×10−7).
evidence: Replicates findings from Ansari et al., 2017 with new data

claim: Novel associations were observed with alanine (p=2.6×10−7) and threonine (p=8.8×10−15) at position 2570 in NS5B in genotype 3a.
source: We also observed novel associations with alanine (p=2.6×10−7) and threonine (p=8.8×10−15) at position 2570 in NS5B, as well as with glycine (p=5.2×10−7) and serine (p=1.04×10−11) at position 2414 in NS5A.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: Novel associations were observed with glycine (p=5.2×10−7) and serine (p=1.04×10−11) at position 2414 in NS5A in genotype 3a.
source: We also observed novel associations with alanine (p=2.6×10−7) and threonine (p=8.8×10−15) at position 2570 in NS5B, as well as with glycine (p=5.2×10−7) and serine (p=1.04×10−11) at position 2414 in NS5A.
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: All the novel associations at positions 2570 and 2414 were only detected in the 3a subgroup.
source: All these associations were only detected in the 3a subgroup.
evidence: Describes the genotype-specificity of the associations

claim: A significant association was observed with histidine at position 2065 of NS5A in patients infected with HCV genotypes 1a (p=9.8×10−7) and 1b (p=1.3×10−7).
source: In concordance with a previous study (Peiffer et al., 2016), we also observed a significant association with histidine at position 2065 of NS5A in patients infected with HCV genotypes 1a (p=9.8×10−7) and 1b (p=1.3×10−7).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results and concordant with Peiffer et al., 2016

claim: Multiple significant associations were observed in the interferon-sensitivity determining region (ISDR, amino acid positions 2209 to 2248 in NS5A) in patients infected with genotype 1b.
source: We also observed multiple significant associations in the interferon-sensitivity determining region (ISDR, amino acid positions 2209 to 2248 in NS5A) in patients infected with genotype 1b, the strongest one being with the presence of leucine at position 2224 (p=1.5×10−12).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: The strongest association in the ISDR region for genotype 1b was with the presence of leucine at position 2224 (p=1.5×10−12).
source: We also observed multiple significant associations in the interferon-sensitivity determining region (ISDR, amino acid positions 2209 to 2248 in NS5A) in patients infected with genotype 1b, the strongest one being with the presence of leucine at position 2224 (p=1.5×10−12).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: For genotype 1a, a single significant association was observed in the ISDR region with the presence of leucine at position 2211 (p=2.8×10−6).
source: For genotype 1a, we observed a single significant association in the ISDR region with the presence of leucine at position 2211 (p=2.8×10−6).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: The association of IFNL4 genotype with HCV amino acid variables is not dependent on the effect of IFNL4 genotype on viral replication rates.
source: To check whether the association of IFNL4 genotype with HCV amino acid variables could be dependent of the effect of IFNL4 genotype on viral replication rates, we also compared the results from two sets of logistic regression models: one that does and one that does not include HCV viral load as an additional covariate. We did not observe any significant difference in the results of the two models (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by comparison of two regression models with and without viral load as covariate

claim: Pre-treatment viral load was found to be significantly associated (p<0.05) with rs12979860 for all HCV genotypes.
source: Pre-treatment viral load was found to be significantly associated (p<0.05) with rs12979860 for all HCV genotypes, with the rs12979860 T allele consistently associated with lower viral load (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: The rs12979860 T allele is consistently associated with lower viral load across all HCV genotypes.
source: Pre-treatment viral load was found to be significantly associated (p<0.05) with rs12979860 for all HCV genotypes, with the rs12979860 T allele consistently associated with lower viral load (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: The strength of the association p-values between rs12979860 and viral load varied between genotypes due to sample size, but the effect size associated with the T allele was comparable across genotype groups.
source: The strength of the association p-values varied between genotypes due to sample size, but the effect size associated with the T allele was comparable across genotype groups.
evidence: Inference based on comparison of effect sizes across genotypes

claim: Significant associations between viral load and HCV amino acid variables were identified in all viral genotype groups except 4a.
source: We then searched for associations between viral load and HCV amino acid variables. These analyses identified significant associations in all viral genotype groups except 4a (Figure 2).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results shown in Figure 2

claim: In genotype 1a, 9 of 18 amino acids that associated with viral load also associated with rs12979860 genotype.
source: Amongst the viral amino acids that associated with viral load, a number also associated with rs12979860 genotype (genotype 1a, 9 of 18 amino acids; 1b, 5 of 17 amino acids; 2a, 0 of 2 amino acids; 2b, 0 of 6 amino acids; 3a, 2 of 3 amino acids).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: In genotype 1b, 5 of 17 amino acids that associated with viral load also associated with rs12979860 genotype.
source: Amongst the viral amino acids that associated with viral load, a number also associated with rs12979860 genotype (genotype 1a, 9 of 18 amino acids; 1b, 5 of 17 amino acids; 2a, 0 of 2 amino acids; 2b, 0 of 6 amino acids; 3a, 2 of 3 amino acids).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: In genotype 3a, 2 of 3 amino acids that associated with viral load also associated with rs12979860 genotype.
source: Amongst the viral amino acids that associated with viral load, a number also associated with rs12979860 genotype (genotype 1a, 9 of 18 amino acids; 1b, 5 of 17 amino acids; 2a, 0 of 2 amino acids; 2b, 0 of 6 amino acids; 3a, 2 of 3 amino acids).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: Higher mean viral load was observed for leucine at position 2224 for both CC and non-CC genotypes of SNP rs12979860 (t-test p-value: 6.2 x10−6 for CC,L vs. CC,non-L; t-test p-value: 4.1 x10−2 for CT,L vs. CT,non-L).
source: This was true for both CC and non CC genotypes of SNP rs12979860 (t-test p-value: 6.2 x10−6 for CC,L vs. CC,non-L; t-test p-value: 4.1 x10−2 for CT,L vs. CT,non-L), indicating a possible impact of that leucine residue on viral replication (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by t-test results and shown in Figure 3B

claim: The leucine residue at position 2224 has a possible impact on viral replication.
source: This was true for both CC and non CC genotypes of SNP rs12979860 (t-test p-value: 6.2 x10−6 for CC,L vs. CC,non-L; t-test p-value: 4.1 x10−2 for CT,L vs. CT,non-L), indicating a possible impact of that leucine residue on viral replication (Figure 3B).
evidence: Inference based on the association pattern observed

claim: The study replicated the previously shown association between viral load and the change from a serine to an asparagine at position 2414 in NS5A protein (p=4.5×10−7) in genotype 3a.
source: We also replicated the previously shown (Ansari et al., 2017) association between viral load and the change from a serine to an asparagine at position 2414 in NS5A protein (p=4.5×10−7) in genotype 3a and observed a lower mean viral load for patients with non-CC genotype and presence of serine at position 2414 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Replicates findings from Ansari et al., 2017 with new data

claim: Lower mean viral load was observed for patients with non-CC genotype and presence of serine at position 2414 in genotype 3a.
source: We also replicated the previously shown (Ansari et al., 2017) association between viral load and the change from a serine to an asparagine at position 2414 in NS5A protein (p=4.5×10−7) in genotype 3a and observed a lower mean viral load for patients with non-CC genotype and presence of serine at position 2414 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: Multiple amino acids were significantly associated with residual viral load across genotypes.
source: We observed multiple significantly associated amino acids with residual viral load across genotypes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: A total of 7 amino acids in genotype 1a associated with rs12979860 genotype, viral load and viral load residuals.
source: A total of 7 amino acids in genotype 1a (supplementary file 1) and six amino acids in genotype 1b (supplementary file 2) associated with rs12979860 genotype, viral load and viral load residuals, including again leucine at position 2224 of NS5A in genotype 1b (presidual = 4.9×10−8).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: A total of 6 amino acids in genotype 1b associated with rs12979860 genotype, viral load and viral load residuals.
source: A total of 7 amino acids in genotype 1a (supplementary file 1) and six amino acids in genotype 1b (supplementary file 2) associated with rs12979860 genotype, viral load and viral load residuals, including again leucine at position 2224 of NS5A in genotype 1b (presidual = 4.9×10−8).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: Leucine at position 2224 of NS5A in genotype 1b associated with rs12979860 genotype, viral load and viral load residuals (presidual = 4.9×10−8).
source: A total of 7 amino acids in genotype 1a (supplementary file 1) and six amino acids in genotype 1b (supplementary file 2) associated with rs12979860 genotype, viral load and viral load residuals, including again leucine at position 2224 of NS5A in genotype 1b (presidual = 4.9×10−8).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results

claim: The strongest association within Europeans was observed with the presence of isoleucine at position 2252 of viral protein NS5A in patients infected with HCV genotype 1a (p=1.2×10−24).
source: We further dissected the association signals within the largest ancestry group, Europeans, by running a per genotype analysis within this sample (Figure 3—figure supplement 3). The strongest association was observed with the presence of isoleucine at position 2252 of viral protein NS5A in patients infected with HCV genotype 1a (p=1.2×10−24).
evidence: Supported by statistical analysis results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: The presence or absence of the IFN-λ4 protein has a pervasive impact on HCV.
source: We show that the presence or absence of the IFN-λ4 protein has a pervasive impact on HCV, by describing multiple associations between host and pathogen variants in subgroups defined by viral genotype or human ancestry.
evidence: Inference based on the multiple associations observed across genotypes and ancestries

claim: NS5A protein is required for HCV RNA replication and virus assembly.
source: This protein is required for HCV RNA replication and virus assembly and has been shown to associate with interferon signaling and hepatocarcinogenesis (Nakamoto et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nakamoto et al., 2014

claim: NS5A has been shown to associate with interferon signaling and hepatocarcinogenesis.
source: This protein is required for HCV RNA replication and virus assembly and has been shown to associate with interferon signaling and hepatocarcinogenesis (Nakamoto et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nakamoto et al., 2014

claim: Previous studies have shown strong associations between variants in the ISDR of NS5A and HCV viral load as well as response to IFN-based therapy.
source: Previous studies have also shown strong associations between variants in the ISDR of NS5A and HCV viral load as well as response to IFN-based therapy (Enomoto et al., 1995; Frangeul et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citations to Enomoto et al., 1995 and Frangeul et al., 1998

claim: Some of the strongest associations observed were in and around the ISDR region, suggesting a possible role of these variants in determining the response to IFN-based antiviral treatment.
source: Some of the strongest associations that we observed were in and around this highly variable region, suggesting a possible role of these variants in determining the response to IFN-based antiviral treatment.
evidence: Inference based on the location and strength of associations

claim: Ansari et al. showed that the variant at position 2414 (a change from a serine to asparagine) is associated with an increase in RNA replication using a genotype three replicon assay.
source: Using a genotype three replicon assay, Ansari et al. showed that this later variant - a change from a serine to asparagine at site 2414 - is associated with an increase in RNA replication, which is concordant with our results.
evidence: Supported by citation to Ansari et al. and concordance with current study results

claim: IFN-λ-driven viral adaptation is a part of evolution across HCV genotypes.
source: These results indicate that IFN-λ-driven viral adaptation is a part of evolution across HCV genotypes.
evidence: Inference based on the observation of consistent associations across genotypes

claim: Only a fraction of the host-driven HCV amino acid variants was found to be associated with viral load.
source: Interestingly, only a fraction of the host-driven HCV amino acid variants was found to be associated with viral load, indicating that an integrated association analysis between host and pathogen genome variations can reveal correlations that would go unnoticed in association studies that use more downstream laboratory measurements or clinical outcomes as phenotypes.
evidence: Observation from the data analysis

claim: An integrated association analysis between host and pathogen genome variations can reveal correlations that would go unnoticed in association studies that use more downstream laboratory measurements or clinical outcomes as phenotypes.
source: Interestingly, only a fraction of the host-driven HCV amino acid variants was found to be associated with viral load, indicating that an integrated association analysis between host and pathogen genome variations can reveal correlations that would go unnoticed in association studies that use more downstream laboratory measurements or clinical outcomes as phenotypes.
evidence: Inference based on the comparison of different analytical approaches

claim: IFN-λ polymorphism is the strongest human genetic predictor of spontaneous HCV clearance and response to IFN-based therapy.
source: IFN-λ polymorphism is the strongest human genetic predictor of spontaneous HCV clearance and response to IFN-based therapy.
evidence: Supported by established knowledge from previous studies

claim: IFNL4 is a functional gene that plays a pivotal role in HCV pathogenesis.
source: Our results confirm that IFN-λ4 is a functional gene that plays a pivotal role in HCV pathogenesis.
evidence: Inference based on the pervasive associations observed

claim: The large footprint left by IFNL4 variation on the HCV proteome is a clear indicator of the importance of innate immunity in viral control.
source: The large footprint left by IFNL4 variation on the HCV proteome is indeed a clear indicator of the importance of innate immunity in viral control and of the remarkable capacity of HCV to evolve escape strategies.
evidence: Inference based on the extensive associations observed

claim: HCV has a remarkable capacity to evolve escape strategies.
source: The large footprint left by IFNL4 variation on the HCV proteome is indeed a clear indicator of the importance of innate immunity in viral control and of the remarkable capacity of HCV to evolve escape strategies.
evidence: Inference based on the extensive associations observed

claim: One clear limitation of the study is the impossibility to distinguish between the two haplotypes encoding the IFN-λ4 P70 and S70 isoforms.
source: Because we genotyped the human SNP rs12979860, a reliable marker for the dinucleotide insertion/deletion polymorphism rs368234815, our analyses exclusively focus on the effects of the presence or absence of the IFN-λ4 protein on HCV amino acids and viral load. Therefore, one clear limitation of our study is the impossibility to distinguish between the two haplotypes encoding the IFN-λ4 P70 and S70 isoforms, which have been shown to have distinctive influences on HCV pathogenesis (Ansari, 2018).
evidence: Acknowledged limitation based on the genotyping approach used

claim: The IFN-λ4 P70 and S70 isoforms have been shown to have distinctive influences on HCV pathogenesis.
source: Because we genotyped the human SNP rs12979860, a reliable marker for the dinucleotide insertion/deletion polymorphism rs368234815, our analyses exclusively focus on the effects of the presence or absence of the IFN-λ4 protein on HCV amino acids and viral load. Therefore, one clear limitation of our study is the impossibility to distinguish between the two haplotypes encoding the IFN-λ4 P70 and S70 isoforms, which have been shown to have distinctive influences on HCV pathogenesis (Ansari, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ansari, 2018

claim: The study used a Bonferroni threshold of 4.7 × 10−6 to control for multiple testing.
source: To control for population stratification, we added host and viral covariates in the model and to control for multiple testing we used a Bonferroni threshold of 4.7 × 10−6, which was calculated based on the number of tests performed (more information in the Materials and methods section).
evidence: Describes the statistical methodology used

claim: The analysis was restricted to genotypes 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 3a and 4a, which were present in at least 100 participants.
source: We restricted the analysis to genotypes 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 3a and 4a, which were present in at least 100 participants.
evidence: Describes the inclusion criteria for genotype analysis

claim: The study used an additive logistic model with binary amino acid variables as traits of interest.
source: We performed a separate analysis for each HCV genotype, using an additive logistic model with binary amino acid variables as traits of interest.
evidence: Describes the statistical methodology used

claim: The study added sex, country of origin, self-reported ethnicity, cirrhosis status and prior treatment experience as covariates to control for host population stratification.
source: We assumed an additive model and corrected for host population stratification by adding sex, country of origin, self-reported ethnicity, cirrhosis status and prior treatment experience as covariates.
evidence: Describes the statistical methodology used

claim: The first five phylogenetic principal components were added as covariates to account for residual viral stratification within each HCV genotype.
source: To account for residual viral stratification within each HCV genotype, the first five phylogenetic principal components (Revell, 2009), calculated per HCV gene to account for recombination, were also added as covariates.
evidence: Describes the statistical methodology used

claim: Box-Cox transformation was used to transform the positively skewed viral load distribution into a normally distributed dependent variable.
source: For the viral load GWAS analysis, we used linear regression where the trait of interest was Box-Cox transformed pre-treatment viral load. We used Box-Cox transformation to transform the positively skewed viral load distribution into a normally distributed dependent variable.
evidence: Describes the statistical methodology used

claim: A total of 10,681 tests were performed in the analyses described in the paper.
source: For the analyses described in the paper, we performed a total of 10,681 tests.
evidence: Describes the number of statistical tests performed

claim: The average coverage of >5000 reads per position was obtained for most of the samples.
source: The average coverage of >5000 reads per position was obtained for most of the samples.
evidence: Describes the sequencing depth achieved

claim: Mixtures were reported when present in ≥15% of the viral population.
source: Mixtures were reported when present in ≥15% of the viral population.
evidence: Describes the threshold for reporting viral mixtures

claim: The study samples were collected from treatment naive and experienced patients from >25 countries in North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, and Africa between years 2010 and 2015.
source: All samples included in this analysis are baseline samples collected from treatment naive and experienced patients from >25 countries in North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, and Africa between years 2010 and 2015.
evidence: Describes the sample collection details

claim: Appropriate informed consent was obtained from study participants allowing the current analysis to be performed.
source: Across 82 studies involving >100 sites in many countries, appropriate informed consent was obtained from study participants allowing the current analysis to be performed (Welzel et al., 2017).
evidence: Describes the ethical approval for the study

claim: Study protocols followed the ethical guidelines set in place by the 1975 Declaration of Helsinki.
source: Study protocols followed the ethical guidelines set in place by the 1975 Declaration of Helsinki and were approved by the relevant institutional review board committees.
evidence: Describes the ethical approval for the study

claim: The study provides evidence of pervasive viral adaptation to innate immune pressure during chronic HCV infection.
source: By demonstrating that IFN-λ variation leaves a large footprint on the viral proteome, we provide evidence of pervasive viral adaptation to innate immune pressure during chronic HCV infection.
evidence: Inference based on the extensive associations observed

claim: IFN-λ variation leaves a large footprint on the viral proteome.
source: By demonstrating that IFN-λ variation leaves a large footprint on the viral proteome, we provide evidence of pervasive viral adaptation to innate immune pressure during chronic HCV infection.
evidence: Supported by the multiple associations observed across the viral proteome

claim: The study reports amino acids associated with both IFN-λ polymorphism and HCV load across multiple viral genotypes.
source: We also present association analyses of human and viral variants with HCV viral load, which allows for a better understanding of the connections between genomic variation, biological mechanisms and clinical outcomes.
evidence: Describes the findings of the study
